notes: §1985:IX.4.4.4 GR5: "A file may be opened with the INPUT, OUTPUT, EXTEND, and I-O phrases in the same run unit", and "each subsequent OPEN statement execution for that same file must be preceded by the execution of a CLOSE statement, without the LOCK phrase, for that file". The two violations have their own statuses: §1985:IX.1.3.4 "I-O Status = 41. An OPEN statement is attempted for a file in the open mode" and "I-O Status = 38. A permanent error exists because an OPEN statement is attempted on a file previously closed with lock". FileRegistry.RefusedAsAlreadyOpen answers an OPEN of an open connector through FileConnector.Open's already-open arm (41) before anything of the new request reaches the connector, so the file stays open in its first mode. FileRegistry.CloseWithLock records the lock only when the CLOSE succeeded, and FileRegistry.SharedOpenAttempt refuses every later OPEN of that file with FileStatusCode.FileLocked (38) for the rest of the run unit. The 1985 edition reaches the lock because VersionConformancePass.VisitCloseOption gates CLOSE WITH LOCK as removed in 2023 only, so 85 accepts the phrase; nothing else differs by edition. Probed at --std 85: the four modes open one file in turn after plain CLOSEs; an OPEN I-O or OUTPUT while open answers 41 and the open file keeps its record; after CLOSE WITH LOCK each of the four modes answers 38 (an OUTPUT does not empty the file) and a further CLOSE (42) does not lift it; a CLOSE WITH LOCK of an unopened file (42) locks nothing. The lock is the PHYSICAL FILE's at --std 85 (§1985:II.2: "mean the physical file regardless of the file-name used in the COBOL program"): FileRegistry.CloseWithLock marks PhysicalFileTable.State.ClosedWithLock and SharedOpenAttempt asks FileRegistry.ClosedWithLock of the physical file's state, so an OPEN through another file-name assigned to the same file answers 38 too and an OPEN OUTPUT through it cannot recreate the file (kb/Work PB5210, DialectBehavior.CloseWithLockLocksFileConnector; from 2002 the file connector is locked instead, §2002:14.8.26.3 GR24). The witness opens an indexed file OUTPUT, INPUT, I-O and EXTEND in one run unit and gets 41 for an OPEN without a CLOSE.

next.reason: 1985: reopening a file requires a prior CLOSE 'without the LOCK phrase' (a reopen after CLOSE WITH LOCK gives status 38). 2023 keeps the close-before-reopen rule: §2023:14.9.27.4 GR2 'shall not be open. If it is open, the execution of the OPEN statement is unsuccessful' (status 41, §2023:9.1.13.7 GR1), and §2023:14.9.6.4 GR8 makes any successful CLOSE without UNIT leave the connector not open. The LOCK carve-out is gone: §2023:E.2 lists 'The WITH LOCK phrase of the CLOSE statement and the related File Status of 38' as removed. The first sentence (all four open modes may be used in one run unit) follows from GR4's open modes and is unchanged.
